text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- 60 percent of Austrians do not support civil servants' demand for more money. Civil servants in the Finance Ministry will stage a warning strike on Tuesday morning.

- Austrian Airlines and Lauda Air plan to benefit from synergy effects as quickly as possible and expect to raise profits significantly. Austrian Airlines took over the majority in Lauda Air earlier this year.
- Othmar Karas, conservative general secretary, says the People's Party will claim the job of Chancellor in general elections due in 1999.
- Interior Minister Karl Schloegl plans to amend a draft law aimed at giving the police more power in the fight against organized crime.

- Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, state secretary in the Finance Ministry, says a labour initiative should be started as a counter-weight to European Economic and Monetary Union. He expects elections in France to have no effect on the start of Europe's single currency euro.
- Austria's biggest baker Anker, which was taken over by German baker Mueller-Brot recently, plans to open its shops on Sundays too, even if this means the company will be fined.
- New car registrations fell 12.2 percent in the first third of 1997.
- Austria Salzburg is the new champion in Austria's football league, after its main rival Rapid Vienna lost in the penultimate round.
DIE PRESSE
- Interior Minister Schloegl criticised the judiciary for not having questioned the alleged writer of a letter bomb threat.
- Westdeutsche Landesbank has the option to take over the City of Vienna's voting stake in Bank Austria which is due to be privatised over the next six years, current affairs magazine Profil reports.
- State secretary Ruttenstorfer demands an EU-wide harmonization of taxes.
- 62 percent of the members of Austria's chamber of Economy favour the inroduction of Europe's single currency euro.
- Both postal savings bank PSK and insurer EA Generali will have to pay for a capital increase in Hungary's Postabank which is necessary for the restructuring of the bank.
- Transport Minister Caspar Einem's draft telecommunications law, which will abolish Post & Telekom Austria's telephone monopoly, is ready for discussion.
- Austrian Airlines will start flying to Shanghai as Austrian firms have already started 30 joint-ventures in the region and have invested about 300 million schillings.
KURIER

- The conflict between the government and the opposition parties over the instalment of a parliamentary investigation committee into the affair around the release of alleged Iranian murderers of three Kurdish leaders in Vienna in 1989 might be solved by a meeting of party leaders today.
- At least 1,300 Viennese school students will not get a place as an apprentice.
